outcome: gut microbiota composition (alpha-diversity, beta-diversity, relative abundances of taxa)
infant growth status (length-for-age z-score, weight-for-age z-score, weight-for-length z-score)
cohort: The study included 115 healthy, full-term infants (4-5 months old) who were either exclusively breastfed (n=54) or exclusively formula-fed (n=61).
finding: Infant feeding type (exclusive breast- or formula-feeding) is the primary driver of gut microbiota differences in young infants, and these microbiota differences are associated with observed variations in growth status.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as the second most significant variable influencing gut microbiota composition, after feeding type.
